# Dhātubhājanīyakathā (Bv 29)

**ID:** Bv 29
**Section:** Buddhavaṁsa (bv)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Dhātubhājanīyakathā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0511m.mul28.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhātubhājanīyakathā* ("The Distribution of the Relics") is the twenty-ninth and concluding chapter of the *Buddhavaṁsa* (Bv 29). The text recounts the dispersal of the Buddha Gotama's bodily relics following his *parinibbāna* at Kusinārā [Skilling, Ideology of relics]. It opens by declaring that after the Buddha was extinguished at Kusinārā, his relics were distributed across diverse locations (verse 1) [Skilling, Ideology of relics]. Verses 2–12 list the specific relics and their enshrining locations, concluding in verse 13 with the observation that the ancient masters (*porāṇakā*) recorded this distribution of the Great Sage Gotama's relics out of compassion for living beings [Skilling, Ideology of relics].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Mentioned in: DN 16 (PTS DN ii 72) Mahāparinibbāna Sutta

**Sources**

- [Skilling, Ideology of relics] Peter Skilling, The ideology of relics in Buddhism — Content breakdown, quoting verses 1 and 13 and noting the enumeration of relics in verses 2–12 as found in connection with the Thūpavaṁsa.
